nodes.label: Extraction Cache (Step B0)
nodes.rationale: Cache entries are stamped with the prompt file that produced them so a changed extraction prompt re-extracts instead of replaying stale results (#1939).

nodes.label: #479 Shrink Guard
nodes.rationale: to_json refuses to write a smaller graph.json than the existing one, preventing an empty/partial extraction from silently clobbering a good graph.

nodes.label: Supabase as Single Source of Truth
nodes.rationale: The Express backend exists only to proxy OpenAI calls and keep the API key server-side; all other data lives directly in Supabase, accessed from the frontend.
nodes.norm_label: supabase as single source of truth

nodes.label: SAFE_CANDIDATE_FIELDS excludes email/linkedin
nodes.rationale: Email and LinkedIn are withheld from GPT to avoid leaking PII into the LLM prompt, but are included when returning candidates directly to the recruiter who needs to contact them.

nodes.label: FASE 1: Normalización de Esquema BD
nodes.rationale: Reconciles candidate status/source enums across DB, backend and frontend, and prepares NOT NULL company scoping for search_history before authorization work begins.

nodes.label: Summary of Key Decisions
nodes.rationale: Consolidates the trade-offs behind the plan: 3-state status enum matching the spec, lowercase source enum for consistency, n8n-based interview automation to avoid Google OAuth in the backend, and defense-in-depth server-side route protection.

nodes.label: FASE 0 Correcciones (migrations 007-009)
nodes.rationale: Fixes candidate source/status enums and adds audit tables before any dependent phase runs, since a wrong enum value would violate DB CHECK constraints downstream (e.g. n8n-webhook.ts inserting 'Web scraping').

nodes.label: FASE 1 Correcciones (apply portal removal + enum fixes)
nodes.norm_label: fase 1 correcciones (apply portal removal + enum fixes)

nodes.label: FASE 5 Correcciones (en_contacto status, not contratacion)
nodes.rationale: 'en_contacto' means the recruiter reached out for interview confirmation, distinct from a future 'contratacion' (hired) state; using the wrong value breaks the status CHECK constraint.

nodes.label: C1: n8n Webhook Sin Autenticación
nodes.rationale: The anon key is public by design, so RLS is the real security boundary, not the frontend; the n8n webhook is mounted without auth and trusts a client-supplied company_id, allowing arbitrary candidate injection.

nodes.label: C2: profiles sin RLS → escalada de privilegios
nodes.rationale: Every RLS policy in the system resolves company scope by reading profiles.company_id; without RLS on profiles a user could rewrite their own role or company_id and defeat multi-tenant isolation entirely.
nodes.norm_label: c2: profiles sin rls → escalada de privilegios

nodes.label: company_candidates bridge table
nodes.rationale: Status is modeled as an attribute of the relationship between a candidate and a company (not of the person), so one candidate can be 'en_contacto' at company A and 'rechazado' at company B without duplication.

nodes.label: Estrategia de Transición (deuda técnica deliberada)
nodes.rationale: candidates is kept alive during the migration because chat, Kanban, reports and six RLS policies already depend on it and are tested; breaking it all at once is deliberately avoided in favor of a later unification migration.
